items.title: "Wooden Joe" Nicholas Interview, 1956-11-12
items.q: Oh, did you ever hear Charlie McCurdy much? How was he on clarinet? Well, he was great. You know, he was playing nothing but strictly music, you know, and make all kinds of sweet – really harmonious stuff. He was good.

ctx.x: Oh, Ernest Rogers. You know, he died, didn't you? Yes. In the short time. Yes. In September. I wanted to go to see him. I didn't know he did till the way after. I went to the funeral, but I didn't see him before. I'm sorry I didn't. Big strong looking, help the fella. Yeah.

Ernest Rogers did. That whole band is gone. What used to play there on Ronald Cronin. Ernest Rogers. I don't see how it's done. I don't get nothing about him anymore. The last Cronin that was playing there. I believe Charlie loved playing Cronin tonight.
Oh, yes. Charlie was playing there. He had his teeth pulled out this spring too, but I think he had his teeth this time.
